entities.whatIs: Las Vegas is supplied mainly by Lake Mead water through SNWA and LVVWD. The roughly 10% groundwater share is pumped from the Las Vegas Valley aquifer, beneath the valley—not from a second river. LVVWD also stores surplus treated river water by injecting it into that aquifer.

servedContext.text: LVVWD also banks surplus treated Colorado River water by injecting it into the Las Vegas Valley aquifer (artificial recharge), and by leaving groundwater unpumped (in-lieu recharge). SNWA’s 2026 plan reports approximately 342,000 acre-ft stored in the Southern Nevada Water Bank through 2024. These are stored credits, not the city’s annual supply share.

SNWA also banks water in Arizona and California. Through 2024 the plan reports approximately 614,000 acre-ft in Arizona and 330,225 acre-ft in California. Arizona recovery is an exchange: Arizona uses banked groundwater and forgoes river water, allowing SNWA to divert that amount at Lake Mead—not a pipeline pumping Arizona groundwater to Las Vegas.

entities.whatIs: Bear Lake is a natural freshwater lake on the Idaho–Utah border in the Western United States. About 109 square miles (280 km2) in size, it is split about equally between the two states; its Utah portion comprises the second-largest natural freshwater lake in Utah, after Utah Lake. The lake has been called the "Caribbean of the Rockies" for its unique turquoise-blue color, which is due to the refraction of calcium carbonate (limestone) deposits suspended in the lake. Its water properties have led to the evolution of several unique species of fauna that occur only within the lake. Bear Lake is at least 250,000 years old and could be several million years old. It was formed by fault subsidence that continues today, slowly deepening the lake along the eastern side. In 1911 the majority of the flow of the Bear River was diverted into Bear Lake via Mud Lake and a canal from Stewart Dam, ending 11,000 years of separation between the lake and that river system.
entities.inflowException: Bear Lake is connected to the Bear River through engineered inlet/outlet canals and pumping, not a reservoir across the main river. Small natural tributaries are outside this river-scale layer.

The shoreline consists of 117 miles (188 km). Much of the water used to serve the 335,000 acre (1360 km2) North Platte Project is stored here. Some of the water in the reservoir is released to satisfy other water rights and to operate power plants downstream of the reservoir. Much of the Pathfinder Reservoir is included in the Pathfinder National Wildlife Refuge. Pathfinder Reservoir is the site of the only established population of the Macedonian Ohrid Trout (S. letnica) in the United States.

entities.whatIs: The Salton Sea is a shallow, landlocked, highly saline endorheic lake in Riverside and Imperial counties in Southern California. It lies on the San Andreas Fault within the Salton Trough, which stretches to the Gulf of California in Mexico. The lake is about 15 by 35 miles at its widest and longest. A 2023 report put the surface area at 318 square miles (823.6 km2). The Salton Sea became a resort destination in the 20th century, but saw die-offs of fish and birds in the 1980s due to contamination from farm runoff, and clouds of toxic dust in the 21st century as evaporation exposed parts of the lake bed.

Including the sand dunes and former beaches of prehistoric Lake Lahontan, the sink is over 1000 sq mi. It is located in northern Churchill County, northwest of Fallon. Today the sink is currently fed by drainage canals of the Truckee-Carson Irrigation District. The southeastern fringe of the sink, where the canals enter, is a wetland of the Central Basin and Range ecoregion characterized by shallow artificial lakes and sloughs called the Stillwater Marsh.

facts.label: Full annual contractor allocation

facts.label: Azotea Tunnel length
facts.quote: The 12.8-mile-long concrete-lined Azotea Tunnel, with a capacity of 950 cubic feet per second, conveys water from Navajo River to Azotea Creek in the Rio Grande Basin.

facts.label: Azotea Tunnel capacity
facts.quote: The 12.8-mile-long concrete-lined Azotea Tunnel, with a capacity of 950 cubic feet per second, conveys water from Navajo River to Azotea Creek in the Rio Grande Basin.

facts.label: Heron Reservoir capacity
facts.quote: The dam is an earthfill structure 269 feet high which forms a reservoir with a capacity of 401,320 acre-feet and a surface area of 5,950 acres.

facts.label: Santa Fe annual availability
facts.quote: Santa Fe’s water availability from the San Juan-Chama Project is 5,230 acre-feet per year, dependent on water availability in the San Juan watershed.

facts.label: Albuquerque surface water treatment capacity
facts.publisher: Albuquerque Bernalillo County Water Utility Authority
facts.quote: The plant, with a capacity of about 80 million gallons per day, uses a series of chemical and mechanical processes to remove sediment and other contaminants from the water.

Adams Tunnel. On the east side it drops through power plants, tunnels and canals to Horsetooth Reservoir and Carter Lake, which supply northern Front Range cities and farms.

facts.label: Average annual supplemental delivery
facts.quote: The Colorado-Big Thompson (C-BT) Project collects, stores and delivers on average 200,000 acre-feet of supplemental water each year.

facts.label: Adams Tunnel length
facts.quote: As the linchpin of the C-BT Project, the 13.1-mile Alva B. Adams Tunnel carries water from the Upper Colorado River Basin beneath Rocky Mountain National Park to users on Colorado’s East Slope.

facts.label: Adams Tunnel capacity
facts.quote: With a capacity of 550 cubic feet per second, the tunnel delivers more than 200,000 acre-feet of water annually to Northeastern Colorado, with travel time through the tunnel averaging about two hours.

facts.label: Adams Tunnel elevation drop
facts.quote: A 109-foot elevation drop between the portals allows water to flow by gravity without pumping.

facts.label: Adams Tunnel diameter
facts.quote: The concrete-lined, cylindrical tunnel measures 9 feet 9 inches in diameter and reaches depths of up to 3,800 feet beneath the Continental Divide.

facts.label: Municipal recipients
facts.quote: A total of 32 municipalities receive a portion of their water through the C-BT Project, along with 120 ditch, reservoir and irrigation companies.

facts.label: Average annual marketed hydropower
facts.quote: Through the U.S. Department of Energy, the Western Area Power Administration markets 700 million kilowatt hours on average each year.

entities.operator: Northern Water and Bureau of Reclamation (joint operation and maintenance of the federally owned project)

entities.whatIs: Denver Water brings water from the Colorado River side of the Divide two ways: Blue River water stored in Dillon Reservoir goes through the 23-mile Roberts Tunnel to the North Fork of the South Platte, and Fraser River water goes through the Moffat Tunnel to South Boulder Creek and Gross Reservoir.

facts.label: Dillon Reservoir storage capacity
facts.quote: Dillon is Denver Water’s largest storage reservoir, capable of holding 257,304 acre-feet of water.

facts.label: Blue River basin share of Denver annual supply
facts.quote: The Blue River basin, which feeds Dillon Reservoir, also provides an average of 30 percent of Denver’s annual water supply, enough water for 320,000 homes every year.

facts.label: Roberts Tunnel delivery capability
facts.value: more than 480 million gallons of water a day
facts.quote: Completed in 1962, the tunnel took 16 years to build and can deliver more than 480 million gallons of water a day to the Front Range.

facts.label: Moffat Tunnel collection streams
facts.quote: The Moffat Tunnel carries water, collected from 36 Grand County streams, and funnels it under the Continental Divide to be stored in Gross Reservoir before going to treatment plants in the metro area.

facts.quote: In partnership with the Strawberry Valley Project (SVP), constructed by Reclamation in the early 1900’s, the Diamond Fork System also conveys 61,500 acre-feet of SVP water for a total annual average of 163,400 acre-feet of trans-mountain water deliveries.

facts.label: Granite Reef dam height

facts.label: Granite Reef construction completion

facts.label: Roosevelt Lake storage description

facts.label: Lahontan spillway-level storage capacity

facts.label: Lahontan storage with flashboards

facts.label: Truckee Canal length

facts.label: Farmland supplied

facts.label: Canal and drainage network
